These components support dynamic simulations of steady-state and transient conditions, such as load changes and switching events. 3.2.2 Additional Model Requirements Given the diverse data center power system architectures, additional custom model development might be required for: • Transformers in medium-voltage power plane architectures, where the integration of BESS and pooled IT and cooling loads creates complex interactions • Specialized transformer configurations found in distributed redundant 4N/3 power distribution or designs involving medium-voltage-level backup power connections • Transformer protections tailored for rapid fault response and load transfer schemes unique to data center power redundancy approaches • Integrating transformer models with complex transfer switch logic and protection schemes, as seen in modern hyperscale data centers • Capturing the impact of combined IT and cooling load feeding from a common medium- voltage bus, which requires coordinated transformer behavior modeling. Custom models should ensure compatibility with dynamic load changes from AI workloads, on- site generation, and demand flexibility strategies prevalent in evolving data center designs. 3.3 Information Technology Loads IT load models need to represent typical power consumption dynamics of the server and network hardware, including: • Time-varying load transitions from idle to peak demand with rapid ramp capabilities • Load sensitivity to voltage and frequency variations. 3.3.1 Standard PSCAD Models Available PSCAD offers generic composite and resistive load components that can approximate aggregated IT loads.
